findings.evidence: Lines 140–152 explicitly unfold the Hodge bundle to apply `tmulConj_baseChange`; line 59 covers only inputs `z ⊗ₜ v`.
findings.fix: Add a general theorem, preferably `[simp]`, stating `(complexificationConjugation V).toEquiv x = tmulConj V x`, and use it instead of unfolding the definition.
findings.issue: `complexificationConjugation` is characterized only on pure tensors; arbitrary-vector reasoning must unfold the bundle, as the `change ... tmulConj` uses at lines 141 and 152 demonstrate.

findings.evidence: Lines 132–135 provide only `map eigenspace(I) = eigenspace(-I)`, while both eigenspaces are public components at lines 218 and 226.
findings.fix: Add the parallel `[simp]` theorem mapping the `-i`-eigenspace to the `i`-eigenspace, derived using involutivity and the existing theorem.
findings.issue: The public theorem says conjugation exchanges the two eigenspaces but exposes only the map from the `i`-eigenspace to the `-i`-eigenspace.

summary: The bundled conjugation lacks a general accessor theorem, forcing consumers to unfold its implementation, and its eigenspace API exposes only one direction of the advertised exchange.
